ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $6.61 cancellation fee (of which $4.50 is payable to the driver); inform the rider the fee stands under NS-1 because the arrival tap and >3-minute wait are confirmed on the system records. No account action.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show dispute, so NS-0 routes it to NS-1 for the driver's no-show claim [F4][NS-0]. The arrival was a driver tap, not a platform auto-confirmation: the timeline separately records the platform arrival log at 14:03:20 [F5] and the driver's own "I'm Here" tap at 14:06:15 [F6], so NS-1(i) is satisfied on the driver_tap branch [NS-1].

NS-1(ii) requires that GPS placed the driver at the pick-up location at the moment of the tap. The trace marks this ✓: at the tap the driver was 178 m from the pickup point, inside the data-layer 200 m arrival radius, with a closest approach of 40 m at 14:03:50 [F6][F1][NS-1]. Nothing in NS-1 fixes the measurement at the pin rather than the pick-up location area, and the rider's argument that the pin/entrance coordinates differ from the driver's 179 m stationary position is not established anywhere in the fact table [F3][F10][NS-1].

NS-1(iii) requires continuous waiting at the pickup for more than 3 minutes after the tap until cancellation. The GPS trace covers the wait without a break [F2][F6][NS-1], and after the 14:06:15 tap the driver stayed within 200 m for 3 min 40 s (220 s > 180 s) until he cancelled at 14:09:55 [F6][F4][NS-1]. The stationary block of 4 min 0 s at 14:05:55–14:09:55 [F3] is consistent with that wait, and F2 shows 5 min 55 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation [F2][NS-1]. All three NS-1 conditions therefore hold, the $6.61 cancellation fee stands, and NS-2 (which only applies where any of (i)–(iii) fails) is not triggered [F4][F7][NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's post-trip statement that he was parked at the pickup and waited more than 3 minutes [F13] is consistent with the system records rather than displacing them [F3][F6][NS-1]. The rider's message "I'm at the entrance, I don't see you" [F10] shows she did not reach the car the driver announced "at the side road" [F9], but the record does not show the driver left the pick-up area, and the fee's conditions are met on the records [F9][F10][NS-1].

No separate waiting-fee item exists in this case: F7 lists only the $6.61 cancellation fee and no $5.00 waiting fee was charged [F7][NS-6]. NS-6 therefore has nothing to waive and no fee_waived outcome arises [F4][F7][NS-6]. NS-7's 30-day window and voucher form govern a refund that does not arise here, since the charge is valid [F4][F7][NS-7]. RD-6 does not apply: no refund is due and no RD-1 violation is recorded, so no account flag is warranted — the driver's profile (including 1 upheld no-show dispute in 90 d) is only ever an additional-action basis and cannot decide this case [F18][RD-6].

rejected_claims.reason: NS-1(ii) is satisfied on the system records: the 14:06:15 'I'm Here' tap placed the driver 178 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m arrival radius, and the policy does not measure this at the pin [F6][F1][NS-1].

The rider's 'I'm at the entrance, I don't see you' [F10] and the driver's 'at the side road' [F9] show the rider did not come to the announced car; nothing in the record places the driver outside the pick-up area, and the 179 m stationary position [F3] is inside the radius that satisfies NS-1(ii) [F9][F10][NS-1].
Accepted in part: no $5.00 waiting fee appears on the record [F7], so NS-6 has nothing to waive — but this does not disturb the $6.61 cancellation fee, which stands under NS-1 [F7][NS-6].

NS-2 applies only where NS-1 (i), (ii) or (iii) fails; here the tap was made [F6], the driver was 178 m from pickup at the tap [F6], and he waited 220 s (> 180 s) inside the radius until cancelling [F6][F4], so the $6.61 is not refundable [NS-1][NS-2].

The driver's statement [F13] is consistent with the system records rather than contradicted by them: the records place him inside the pick-up radius at the tap and continuously thereafter [F6][F2][F3][NS-1].
No refund is due and no RD-1 violation is recorded, so RD-6's account flag is not triggered; the driver's profile [F18] is only an additional-action basis and cannot decide the case [F18][RD-6].
Accepted as far as it goes — the rider did not board during the wait [F9][F10][F4] — and it supports the finding that NS-1 was satisfied [NS-1].
